av_event.line_text: Not of my own. Claire's got a lad, he's twenty, moved to Bristol last year. Still comes back every Sunday for his dinner, mind. And takes half the fridge back with him.
av_event.what: A woman in a dark work top walks through the kitchen doorway behind him, picks up the kettle from the worktop and walks back out of frame; Darren glances over his shoulder at her briefly while still talking.

text:
A: Alright. Can you hear me okay?
B: Ar. Another Darren. Are there any other names in Taunton, or what?
A: Not many, apparently.
B: My kids' dad's a Darren. You're my second today. It's not your fault, I'm just saying.
A: Fair enough. I'll try and be a better one.
B: You couldn't be worse, honestly. Go on, you're the leisure centre one, are you? Ellie reckoned you looked just like her supervisor.
A: That's me. Duty manager. Did she? Poor girl.
B: She meant it nice. I'm Kelly, Walsall, care home. Part-time. Earlies mostly.
A: Right. Earlies are a killer. I've done a run of six o'clock opens this week, I'm knackered.
B: Six. That's nothing, I'm up at half five for the bus and it still comes late. Every day. You'd think they'd change the timetable to what it actually does.
A: Ha. I drive, but there's roadworks on the A358 that's doing my head in, so I'm not much better off.
B: At least you've got a car. Do you have kids?
A: Not of my own. Claire's got a lad, he's twenty, moved to Bristol last year. Still comes back every Sunday for his dinner, mind. And takes half the fridge back with him.
B: Mine's sixteen and he does that and he still lives with me. I do a big shop, I come home, it's gone. Bread, ham, everything. Do you know what I mean? Where does it go?
A: It doesn't stop at twenty, I can tell you that.
B: Don't tell me that. I'm skint enough as it is.
A: Yeah, sorry.
B: Do you know when this pays out, by the way? Nobody knows. I've asked everyone.
A: No idea, I'm afraid. I'd guess a few weeks. That's about it really.
B: A few weeks. Great. I'm still waiting on a voucher from another one from August.
A: You do a lot of these, then?
B: A few. It's a bit extra, ain't it. Some of them are dead boring, like, rate this yoghurt from one to seven. This one's alright, to be fair, you just talk.
A: Yeah, it's not bad. What's the care side like, then?
B: Hard. My back's gone from hoisting. The residents are lovely, mostly. It's the managers. I'm "mouthy", apparently.
A: Ha. I've got a couple of those on my staff. Usually the ones who are right.
B: See, that's what I say. Nobody listens, though.
A: You've just got to pick your moment, I find. Say it once, say it calm, and then
